A regular hexagon can be divided into six equilateral triangles by drawing lines from the center to each vertex. In this division, the side length of each equilateral triangle is exactly the side length of the hexagon.

Given the perimeter of one equilateral triangle is 21 inches, each side of that triangle is \( 21 \div 3 = 7 \) inches. Therefore, the side length of the regular hexagon is also 7 inches.

The perimeter of a regular hexagon is 6 times its side length:  
\( 6 \times 7 = 42 \) inches.

*Note on the common mistake:* Some solvers mistakenly calculate the perimeter of the hexagon by summing the perimeters of all six triangles and then subtracting the internal edges only once, yielding \( 6 \times 21 - 6 \times 7 = 84 \) inches. This incorrectly counts the internal edges, doubling the correct answer. The correct perimeter is simply the sum of the outer sides of the hexagon.

Answer: 42
